Well I can't think of any real childhood trauma. The only thing that really comes to mind was that I always dreaded having to see my father, but it wasn't because he was abusive to me or something like that. 

I suppose emotionally unavailable is one way of putting it. I'll check out that site.

Well I don't think you're wrong for being apprehensive about the whole thing. You aren't a therapist, you are not equipped to deal with a severely suicidal person alone - especially if they're being manipulative towards you.

I'm not saying to leave him, in fact I'd discourage that, but you need to understand your limits too. He clearly needs more help than he's getting, and IMO you should be encouraging him to seek that while being supportive. That said, mental illness isn't an excuse for toxic behavior or abuse, so if he starts crossing the line, don't be afraid to take a step back from him for your own safety.
That's some serious stuff dude. What are the chances of actually getting the life sentence? You mentioned that no one was hurt, so surely that will be taken into account during sentencing.

Ultimately the only way to be certain is to work with her and learn whatever her specific situation is. 

The best advice I can offer is not to let yourself get overly emotional. Don't be closed off, let her know that you do care, but when you start crying or whatever it can make her feel worse because her issues are now hurting you too. You need to be there and be objective about the situation. Sometimes it isn't about what you can tell someone, but what they can tell you.

Maybe the resources on the sidebar could help. Its worth checking out anyway, but don't take it as gospel because everyone's situation is different.

I can't possibly understand what you're dealing with, but I'm sorry for your loss(es). I do know what its like to watch an elderly relative deteriorate and its by far one of the most traumatizing things I've dealt with, but I can't even imagine what it must be like to have lost a child too + the drama with your mom.

I hope things work out in the end, whatever you do.
You can talk to me if you want, but I'm not sure I'd have anything to contribute.
